line: Crowley’s Ace of Swords: the Root of the Powers of Air, Kether, with Tiphareth as the Ruach’s centre.

sections.title: What Crowley names
sections.line: The chapter heading for the card. The second quotation gives the element of its suit.

quotes.quote: THE ROOT OF THE POWERS OF AIR
“Wands”, attributed to Fire; “Cups”, to Water; “Swords”, to Air;

sections.title: Its place on the Tree
sections.line: The Ace chapter names Kether as the source that descends on Tiphareth, centre of the Ruach. The Aces essay gives Spirit as Kether. No planet-in-sign appears in the chapter.

quotes.quote: Finally, from Kether, the supreme, descends directly
On the other hand, Spirit represents Kether.

sections.title: What it figures
sections.line: Crowley calls the card the primordial Energy of Air, the Essence of the Vau, and says Air is the conjunction of Fire and Water.

quotes.quote: The Ace of Swords is the primordial Energy of Air, the Essence of the Vau of Tetragrammaton
Air is the result of the conjunction of Fire and Water
In nature, the obvious symbol of Air is the Wind
